toc.title: Areas of focus of the key roles

html:
1Purpose, objectives and principles

The quality practice makes sure the project creates products that are fit for purpose and that the users can accept. It starts from the user quality expectations (what the customer side expects) and turns them into acceptance criteria and quality criteria that can be checked.

It serves mainly focus on products: quality is defined product by product before building. It also serves continued business justification (benefits depend on usable products), define roles, responsibilities and relationships (who checks, who assures, who accepts), manage by stages (quality is reviewed at each boundary) and tailor to suit the project.

Exam tip

. Quality is defined before the product is built, not after. If a scenario writes the criteria after the work is finished, the approach is not fit for purpose.

2The key management products

Product What it is for
Product description One product: purpose, composition, derivation, format, quality criteria and how it will be checked and by whom
Product register A record of the products, their status and their approval
Quality management approach How quality will be achieved on this project: standards, methods, roles, records and acceptance. Part of the initiation documentation
Quality register A record of every planned and completed quality check, with who, when and the result

The project product description (Module 5) holds the user quality expectations and acceptance criteria for the whole project.

Exam tip

. Quality register records checks; product register records products and approvals. Pick by the verb: checked and result means quality register, approved and status means product register.

3Areas of focus of the key roles

Role Focus in the quality practice
Executive Quality is affordable and supports the business case
Senior user Gives the user quality expectations and acceptance criteria; provides user reviewers; confirms users accept the products
Senior supplier Supplier standards and quality system are used; products meet the specification
Project manager Plans quality and applies the quality management approach; keeps the records
Team manager Quality control within work packages; reports results
Project assurance Independent checks that the quality approach is followed and working
Project support Maintains the registers

The board gives the final acceptance of the project product at closure. Check the book's table for exact wording.

4Effective management and techniques

Activity What it means
Quality planning Agree expectations, acceptance criteria, quality criteria, tolerances, methods and roles; write product descriptions before work starts
Quality control Check the product against its criteria with tests, inspections or reviews; record results and follow up defects
Quality assurance Independent assessment that the quality approach is followed and will meet needs; not done by the producer
Quality review A planned check of a product by chosen reviewers against its criteria, with recorded findings and follow-up
Acceptance Formal confirmation, by the person named in the product description, that the product meets its acceptance criteria

Quality control happens during delivery. Quality assurance runs alongside the project and reports to the board. Rework needs time in the plan, and approval is recorded in the product register.

Exam tip

. The person who made the product does not judge it. If the author, or the project manager, approves a product for the users, look for the independent reviewer or the senior user.

5Judging a scenario

An effective approach Red flags (not fit for purpose)
Criteria in product descriptions before building (focus on products) Criteria invented after delivery, or only "it works"
Independent reviewers and testers The author checks their own work
Every check recorded in the quality register with result Checks done but not recorded, or recorded only at the end
Acceptance by the right person (senior user for user needs) Project manager or supplier accepts on the users' behalf
Assurance independent of the project manager Project manager assures their own project
Quality checks and rework scheduled in the stage plan Quality squeezed into the last week with no rework time
Findings used for lessons (learn from experience) Same defects repeat stage after stage

Tailoring.

Context How quality changes
Small internal project A short quality approach; one combined register
Agile or hybrid delivery Acceptance criteria on each backlog item; user accepts each increment; team's definition of done is recorded
Large or multi-party project Acceptance criteria in contracts; assurance of each supplier's quality system
Sustainability or data concerns Quality criteria include energy use, materials or data quality and security
Exam tip

. Tailoring scales the paperwork, not the independence. A short quality approach is fine; an unrecorded self-check by the author is not.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A developer in Wei Chen's team tests his own payment component, finds no faults and marks it approved in the product register. There is no other check. Was this appropriate?

  • AYes, because the author knows the product best, so the check is quicker and cheaper to do
  • BYes, because the product register shows the approval, which is all that is needed here
  • CNo, because the author should not judge the product and the check must be recorded
  • DNo, because only the project board may carry out the quality control of any product
Show the answer

Answer: C. Quality control should be independent of the author and recorded in the quality register, as focus on products and assurance require.

S2When Project Harbor closes, who should confirm on behalf of the users that the online permit service meets its acceptance criteria?

  • AAisha Bello, project assurance
  • BLena Kovac, senior supplier
  • CSam Okafor, project manager
  • DTomas Reyes, senior user
Show the answer

Answer: D. The senior user speaks for the users and confirms acceptance; assurance is independent, the supplier built it and the project manager does not accept for users.

S3The build stage is about to start, and the quality management approach requires independent reviews. Sam Okafor finds the stage's product descriptions have no quality criteria. What should he do?

  • AStart the build and let the team write the criteria as each test is run later
  • BGet the criteria written and agreed with users before authorizing any work
  • CAsk project assurance to write the criteria once the products are all complete
  • DDrop the independent reviews so that the stage is not delayed by any checking
Show the answer

Answer: B. Criteria must exist and be agreed before building starts, otherwise quality control has nothing to check against.

S4Sam Okafor wants one record of every planned and completed check on Project Harbor, with dates, reviewers and results. Which management product holds it?

  • AQuality register
  • BProduct register
  • CProduct description
  • DHighlight report
Show the answer

Answer: A. The quality register records each quality check and its result; the product register records products and approvals, and a product description defines one product.

S5Aisha Bello, project assurance, sees that all checks of the payment component were done by the supplier's own team. She tells the board the approach is not independent enough and suggests an independent reviewer. Was this appropriate?

  • AYes, because assurance independently checks the approach and reports concerns to the board
  • BYes, because assurance should take over the team's work and carry out all the tests itself
  • CNo, because only the project manager may raise any quality concerns with the project board
  • DNo, because assurance must wait until the end project report before it comments on quality
Show the answer

Answer: A. Project assurance is an independent check on the approach and reports to the board; it does not take over the team's testing.

S6An agile team on Project Harbor writes acceptance criteria on each backlog item, and Tomas Reyes accepts each increment. Sam Okafor wonders about a separate heavy acceptance document for each item. What should he do?

  • ARequire a separate formal acceptance document for every single item in the backlog
  • BRemove the quality register because the sprints already include a lot of testing
  • CRecord the backlog acceptance in the quality approach and keep the registers current
  • DLet the supplier's team accept its own increments to save time during each sprint
Show the answer

Answer: C. Tailoring adapts the format, so criteria on backlog items and user acceptance can stand if recorded in the approach; the registers and independence remain.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is the purpose of the quality practice?

Show the answer

To create products that are fit for purpose and can be accepted by the users.

R2Which activity checks products against their criteria?

Show the answer

Quality control.

R3Who carries out quality assurance?

Show the answer

Project assurance or another function independent of the team that produces the product.

R4What does the product register record?

Show the answer

The products, their status and their approval.

R5When are acceptance criteria agreed?

Show the answer

Before the products are built.

R6Where is the way quality will be achieved recorded?

Show the answer

In the quality management approach, part of the initiation documentation.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Purpose products fit for purpose and acceptable to users
Product description purpose, composition, quality criteria and how checked
Quality register every planned and completed check with result
Product register products, status and approval
Quality control checks the product, recorded
Quality assurance independent check of the approach
Acceptance by the right person, against criteria set before building
Tailoring scales the paperwork, never the independence
